title: adversarial-review ledger finding record
description: One hypothesis a finder produced. Note what is absent: there is no disposition field. A finding's state is derived from the events appended after it, so nothing in the ledger is ever rewritten and the record of when each state landed survives. Keyword use stays inside the conservative set the bundled validator walks; cross-field rules live in ledger.py.

id.description: F-r<round>-<territory>-<NN>, assigned by the orchestrator in the finder's report order so rank is preserved without a rank field.

quoted_evidence.description: Verbatim code the claim is about. A finding whose evidence is a paraphrase cannot be verified by anyone who did not already believe it.

claim.description: One falsifiable statement of what is wrong and why.

proposed_fix.description: The concrete change. Read at disposition, never shown to the verifier — a verifier who can see the proposed fix is reading the finder's reasoning.

proposed_repro.description: A single read-only or test-runner command that would demonstrate the claim.

claimed_severity.description: Two values on purpose. A finer scale invites the rank inflation this design already refused when it dropped severity promotion on agreement.

reachability.description: What it takes to hit the defect: normal_use, a specific_environment, a hand_edited_input, or unknown when the finder cannot say. A blocker nobody reaches in normal use can be listed rather than fixed inside the loop, and unknown routes as normal_use, so a finder that skips the question gains nothing by it. The routing lives in ledger.py.

failure_mode.description: How the defect shows itself when hit. loud means an error or crash the user sees; silent means wrong output that reads as right. A blocker outside normal use that fails silently still escalates, because nobody will notice it and come back to the listing.
